findings.message: FC-02: Some Reuters text (Doran's quotes, the 'witness came forward' wording, 'police have not named') was seen only as reposted on a forum (TigerDroppings). The ledger marks those passages best-effort and does not count them towards corroboration; P-DORAN rests on them alone.
findings.fix: Open the original Reuters story (2014) and confirm the two Doran quotes word for word, or cut the quote card.

findings.message: FC-03: The Advocate's report that the second witness came forward only after Nodier visited him in jail and threatened him rests on one excerpt. It is an adverse claim about a living person and is attributed on screen and in narration ('The Advocate ... reported').
findings.fix: Read The Advocate's 2014 story in full and confirm the wording, or drop the line and the right-hand side of the split card.

findings.message: P-CEMETERY: conflicting accounts recorded: C02: Funeralwise places the cemetery 'on the grounds of the Toca Plantation'. It is consistent with the location but uses a different name. The Advocate also gives the name 'E.E. Matt Pet Cemetery'. — Handling: Script uses the cemetery's name and Toca; no plantation name.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-GRACE: conflicting accounts recorded: C03: Founding year: 'about 1950' (Advocate) vs 1948 (Mercure). Her surname is given as Grace Thompson (Advocate), Grace Wynne (Funeralwise) and Grace Matt Thompson (Mercure). — Handling: Script says 'around 1950' and 'her mother, Grace'; no surname variants or 1934 history.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-AGE: conflicting accounts recorded: C05: The Advocate gives 63 in one passage and 61 in another. Abandoned Atlas also describes her as 63 and says she was born in 1924, which would make her 60 or 61 in April 1985. | The Advocate excerpt gives 63 in one passage and 61 in another; recorded, not counted as contradicting evidence. — Handling: Script uses 61 (Sheriff's Office, FOX 8, Reuters text); the Advocate's single 63 is recorded, not used.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-VANISH: conflicting accounts recorded: C09: Interval: 'ten days' (FOX 8), 'several days' (Advocate), 'a few days' (AOL). — Handling: Script says 'days before' her court date; no 'ten days'.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-SUFFOCATED: conflicting accounts recorded: C08: Reuters (via forum repost) says she was 'strangled in rural St. Bernard Parish' (see C17). | C17: Suffocated or smothered (SBSO, FOX 8, Advocate) vs strangled (Reuters). — Handling: Attributed to the Sheriff's Office ('suffocated'); the Reuters 'strangled' is recorded, not narrated.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-RIVER: conflicting accounts recorded: C12: 'Fishermen' (FOX 8) vs 'a fisherman' (AOL). — Handling: Script says 'fishermen' and 'steel chains'; the 200-pound figure (HBO material only) is not used.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-PSYCHIC: conflicting accounts recorded: C22: The brief implied a psychic or medium prompted the 2009-2012 reopening. No source says so. The only psychic found is this one, in the early 1980s investigation (see C67). — Handling: Script places the psychic in the early years only; no psychic is linked to the reopening.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-REOPEN: conflicting accounts recorded: C25: One outlet (unidentified) dates the reopening to 2012. FOX 8 (2012) dates the key witness to April 2012. Best reading: reopened 2009, broke open 2012. | Yahoo relays that an unnamed outlet dated the reopening to 2012; that second-hand date is recorded here, not counted as contradicting evidence. — Handling: Script uses 2009 for the reopening and 2012 for the second witness.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-WITNESS1: conflicting accounts recorded: C26: Reuters says 'a witness came forward'. Biography.com and Yahoo say 'an anonymous caller'. Whether the 2009 informant was ever identified is unknown. — Handling: Script says 'a man contacted police' (Reuters: a witness; others: an anonymous caller); the ghost is his claim, as Doran described it.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-WITNESS2: conflicting accounts recorded: C28: FOX 8 says the witness came forward in April 2012. SBSO says 'in the months before the arrest' (April 2012). This is a small timing mismatch. — Handling: The witness is not named (police did not name him).
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-SILENCE: conflicting accounts recorded: C30: '28 years' does not fit 1985 to 2012 exactly (27 years). Treat it as approximate. — Handling: Not used in the script.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-WHY-GHOST: conflicting accounts recorded: C31: The Advocate gives a different, earthly reason for coming forward: Nodier threatened him in jail (C32). Both accounts may be partly true. Present both. — Handling: Both reasons are given, each attributed.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-WHY-THREAT: conflicting accounts recorded: C32: Conflicts with the ghost explanation in C31 (Biography.com, Yahoo, HBO). — Handling: Both reasons are given side by side, each attributed (he said / The Advocate reported); the film does not choose between them.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-PLEA: conflicting accounts recorded: C39: The FOX 8 lead and a Ranker list say 'murder'. The charge pleaded to was manslaughter. Biography.com says 'convicted' without naming the charge. | C41: The apparent 2026 date comes from the date of a forum repost (about 2026-02-27) of an older Reuters story. Ages (58 in 2012, 60 at the plea), '29 years', Biography.com's 'July 2014' and AOL's '2014' all point to 2014. The exact day is NOT verified. July 2014 rests on Biography.com alone; SBSO and Reuters say only that it was a Friday. — Handling: Script says 'in 2014'; the exact day is not used.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-IN-COURT: conflicting accounts recorded: C39: The FOX 8 lead and a Ranker list say 'murder'. The charge pleaded to was manslaughter. Biography.com says 'convicted' without naming the charge. — Handling: Script says manslaughter, never murder, for the plea.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-1970: conflicting accounts recorded: C49: RogerEbert.com's summary of the series mentions a death 'closed as a suicide despite the victim having been shot twice in the back' (C55). That does not match a self-defence finding and may refer to a different death. — Handling: Stated with the self-defence finding; the husband is not named (one source only).
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-ROBINSON: conflicting accounts recorded: C52: The search tool, not the article, labelled this a '1978 death'. RogerEbert.com refers to a death 'closed as a suicide' (C55). Whether that is Robinson's death is unknown. — Handling: Stated with 'no charges were filed'; no manner-of-death claim; the review's 'suicide' line is not used.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-HBO: conflicting accounts recorded: C60: The WBD listing also carried an unexplained 'October 13' line. | C61: Spelling: 'Philip' (most outlets) vs 'Phillip' (WWNO result). — Handling: Spelling 'Philip Cairney' (most outlets).
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: P-WHEREABOUTS: conflicting accounts recorded: C46: No release record found. Unrelated people share the name Brandon Nodier: a college football player and a business-directory listing in Arabi. Do not conflate them. — Handling: Script says whereabouts unknown, attributed to Biography.com; no same-name records are used.
findings.fix: Re-check the handling note if the script changes.

findings.message: FC-01: Every source was read as a search excerpt. nola.com, wdsu.com and reuters.com could not be reached, and no page was opened in full. 23 claims are CORROBORATED by two or more independent publishers; 7 high-risk legal claims therefore cannot reach the DIRECTLY SUPPORTED level the gate requires.
findings.fix: Before publication, read in full: The Advocate's 2014 plea story, the St. Bernard Parish Sheriff's Office plea post, and FOX 8's 2012 and 2014 reports. Record the passages with access level full_text.

findings.message: LR-01: Brandon Nodier is alive and is shown as an illustrated figure (not a likeness): at work on the grounds (as a 1985 groundskeeper) and standing in court in 2014. He is never shown doing any act, and he is never called a murderer or killer.
findings.fix: Keep. If the owner prefers, swap his figure for a silhouette as well.

findings.message: LR-02: Police did not name the second witness; some outlets (Biography.com, Yahoo) do. The film does not name him and shows witnesses only as silhouettes.
findings.fix: Keep it that way in the description, comments and any Shorts.

findings.message: LR-03: Two events in the victim's own past (a 1970 shooting ruled self-defence; a later husband found shot with no charges) are in the research but single-source and adverse to her. They are not used.
findings.fix: Use only if read in full from an official source, and with the official outcome attached.

findings.message: LR-04: The title uses HBO's series name, 'The Pet Cemetery Murders'. The only conviction is for manslaughter. The film says so directly ('Its title says murders. The legal record says manslaughter.'), and the description and pinned comment state the plea.
findings.fix: Keep the legal-status paragraph at the top of the description.

findings.message: AUD-01: The pronunciation of 'Nodier' is not verified. The narration uses 'No-dee-ay' (French). Speech recognition heard 'No D.I.' or 'NoDI'. Locals may say it differently.
findings.fix: Owner to listen to the names sample; if it is wrong, change the pronounce entry and make a new versioned cut.

findings.message: AUD-02: The voice-to-music ratio under speech is 19.4 dB over the whole film, just under the 20 dB aim; the opening minute is higher (see narration-qa.md).
findings.fix: If the owner hears the music competing on a phone, lower music_db by 1–2 dB in the next cut.
